module_title: Historical Background, Making of the Constitution & Preamble - Basic Understanding
introduction: The Indian Constitution was not created overnight; it evolved through various British Acts and was finally drafted by a dedicated Constituent Assembly. The 'Preamble' serves as the introduction or preface to this massive document, summarizing its core philosophy and goals.

core_concepts.title: Demand for a Constitution
core_concepts.description: The idea of a Constituent Assembly for India was first put forward by M.N. Roy in 1934. It was finally accepted by the British in the 'Cabinet Mission Plan' of 1946, under which the assembly was formed.

core_concepts.title: The Drafting Committee
core_concepts.description: Among all the committees of the Constituent Assembly, the most important was the Drafting Committee set up on August 29, 1947. It consisted of 7 members and was chaired by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar.

core_concepts.title: Adoption vs. Enforcement
core_concepts.description: The Constitution was adopted on November 26, 1949 (celebrated as Constitution Day). However, it fully came into force on January 26, 1950 (celebrated as Republic Day) to commemorate the 'Purna Swaraj' declaration of 1930.

core_concepts.title: The Preamble
core_concepts.description: The Preamble begins with 'We, the people of India', indicating that the source of the Constitution's authority is the people. It declares India to be a Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic, and Republic state.

important_entities.name: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar
important_entities.significance: As the Chairman of the Drafting Committee, he played the most crucial role in giving final shape to the Constitution.

important_entities.name: Dr. Rajendra Prasad
important_entities.significance: He was elected as the permanent President of the Assembly and later became the first President of independent India.

important_entities.name: M.N. Roy
important_entities.significance: The first person to officially propose the idea of a Constituent Assembly for India in 1934.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Students often confuse the dates. Remember: Adopted/Enacted = Nov 26, 1949. Enforced/Came into effect = Jan 26, 1950.

Dr. Rajendra Prasad was the permanent president, but the first *temporary/interim* president of the assembly was Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha (following the French practice of electing the oldest member).

mnemonics_and_tricks.trick_title: Nature of Indian State in Preamble
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic, Republic. Always remember this exact sequence as it is frequently asked.

exam_strategy_tips: Memorize the exact date of the first meeting of the Constituent Assembly: December 9, 1946.
Questions directly asking who the Chairman of the Drafting Committee was (Dr. Ambedkar) are staples in basic exams.
